_comment: Single source of truth of the inbox domain: agent IDs, models, connector, tool names (verified live 2026-09-23 via connectors.list_tools), label vocabulary and limits. Python (workflows/src/workflows/inbox/config.py) reads from here. The gmail tool names are the LIVE ones (search_threads, create_draft, label_*), NOT the older names that were once in crm.json. Note two field names that are not what one would guess and cost a day: list_labels returns 'labelId' (not 'id'), and create_label requires 'displayName' (not 'name').

measurement._comment: Numbers next to the setting they justify (golden rule 6). evalkit + cascade eval, 8 constructed cases, 2026-09-24. Rubric revision: B and E require 'recognised as time-critical' (forbidden: whenever), not the exact bucket — today vs this_week is sorting, not an error.

cascade_final.finding: The second stage re-rolls correct first-stage answers too (case F).

history.step: urgency rule sharpened to calendar dates
rubric made honest (B/E: bucket -> time-critical) + context bonus forbidden

measurement.decision: First stage small/none triages everything. The medium second stage STAYS: on the first real run it removed a systematic first-stage error (threaded 'Re:' read as correspondence, 5 of 50) that no constructed case had predicted. The constructed-case verdict ('the cascade scores below its own first stage') did not survive contact with real mail. The kill switch second_review_changed keeps counting, but it now compares InboxReview.verdict() instead of the whole answer — comparing everything counted a reworded 'reasoning' as a change and could never read zero. Reasoning helped here (medium/high 100%), unlike the earlier finding in the book domain.

first_real_run.finding: The first stage alone classified 5 of 50 mails as 'correspondence' — all five machine mail (4 GitHub 'Re:' threads, 1 automated waitlist invite). It reads a threaded 'Re:' subject as a conversation. With the second stage: 0. Since 'correspondence' routes to NEEDS_REPLY in the cleanup plan, those five would have been labelled 'reply owed' instead of archived as noise.
first_real_run.second_review_changed: 9/9 verdicts, of which 5 substantive on inspection
first_real_run.verdict: The second stage EARNS its place — the opposite of what the constructed cases suggested (cascade 95% vs first stage 98%). Nobody constructed a GitHub 'Re:' thread. Keep it; revisit after a week.
